intro.title: Controlled Input
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive form with an input field that displays and updates user-entered text in real-time. You'll learn the concept of controlled inputs, where Angular components manage the input's value through two-way data binding instead of letting the DOM handle it directly. The core programming concept involves using Angular's reactive forms or template-driven forms to bind input values to component properties, ensuring your application state stays synchronized with user input. You'll work with Angular's FormControl, reactive forms, and data binding techniques to create inputs that respond immediately to user changes. By the end, you'll understand how controlled inputs provide better data validation, state management, and user experience in Angular applications.
intro.usecase: Controlled inputs are fundamental to building interactive web applications where user data needs to be validated, formatted, or synchronized in real-time. You'll find this pattern in login forms that validate email formats as users type, search bars that filter results instantly, settings panels where changes update live previews, and checkout forms that calculate totals based on quantity inputs. Modern applications like Slack's message composer, GitHub's issue creation form, and Netflix's search interface all rely on controlled inputs to provide immediate feedback and maintain consistent application state as users interact with form fields.
